item.itunes:title: 淪陷區可以選市長嗎？Can You Actually Vote for Your Mayor in China?#926 @mynotebook
item.itunes:author: 我的學習筆記-王苡儒
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zXsWQVNUCrY

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析兩岸地方治理架構的本質差異，揭開中共體制下「市委書記」與「市長」之間權力階級的神秘面紗。
  • 透過生動的企業職位比喻與「三重一大」制度解說，讓艱澀的「黨政雙軌制」運作邏輯與決策流程變得易於理解。
  • 反思集權動員與民主問責的制度代價，探討「權力授權來源」如何決定官員究竟是「唯上是從」還是「以民為本」。

摘要

市長為何只是二把手？拆解黨政雙軌制

在自由地區，地方首長由公民直選產生並全權掌握地方資源；然而在中國大陸的政治體制中，表面上風光剪綵、掌握預算的市長，實質上僅是「二把手」，真正的「一把手」是市委書記。說故事的人指出，市長代表負責執行的政府行政機關，而市委書記則代表掌控政治方向與人事大權的共產黨委員會。用現代企業來比喻，市委書記好比兼任朝廷監軍的「董事長」，市長則只是負責幹活的「總經理兼CEO」，體現了體制內「管錢的永遠搞不過管人的」之現實。

三重一大與體制微表情：黨大於政的運作現實

這套階級機制並非潛規則，而是明文寫在名為「三重一大」的制度規範中。任何重大決策、重要人事、重大項目與大額資金，即便市政府完成詳盡的調研與規劃，也必須送交市委常委會接受政治把關，形成「政府調研提案、黨委拍板定案、政府苦幹執行、黨委在後監工」的權力循環。此外，官方新聞中的排序先後、座次安排等「體制微表情」，更隨時都在向外界宣示「黨大於政」的核心原則。

極致效率背後的死穴：一言堂、內耗與權責分離

黨政雙軌制雖具備「集中力量辦大事」的高動員力與推土機般的效率，卻也帶來難以抹滅的制度代價。首先是一把手權力失控，如同薄熙來時期的重慶模式，政治意識碾壓專業技術；其次是若黨政兩大領導不合，易陷入嚴重的派系內耗；更關鍵的是「權責分散」的甩鍋死結——決策是由閉門的黨委會拍板，司法與外部無從監督，但行政執行與日後的爛攤子、法律責任卻主要由行政首長承擔，外界難以釐清真實責任歸屬。

權力向誰負責：民主授權與民權主義的終極反思

說故事的人強調，兩套制度最根本的差異在於「授權方向」。自由地區首長的權力直接來自選民，做不好隨時會被選票拉下台；而對岸官員的政治前途取決於上級黨委的臉色，導致其決策必然「唯上是從」而非「以民為本」。這正呼應了國父孫中山先生所提出的「政權在民，治權在府」。唯有當地方首長的權力真正來自人民、只需看人民臉色時，才能走出體制怪圈，落實真正的共和與民權價值。

================================================

哈囉大家好。我是阿牛哥。今天要繼續來聊聊。兩岸制度上的差異。

今天想要跟大家聊的是。地方首長。在我們的自由地區。大家已經很習慣了。地方首長是由人民直選的。可以掌握整個地方的資源。但是在淪陷區就不是這樣。表面上市長去風光剪綵。出席活動。回到了辦公室。卻要看另外一個人的臉色。也就是市委書記。那問題來啦。

為什麼名義上是市府的最高長官。但卻只是二把手呢？在災區的權力架構裡。市長代表的是行政機關。也就是政府的系統。但市委書記。他代表的是共產黨委員會。也就是黨的系統。依照他們的規矩。黨是管方向、管人事、管大局的。政府只是負責執行黨的決策。而且這個黨領導政府。不是阿牛哥故意酸他們。更不是什麼官場上的潛規則。中共自己黨內法規。就把地方黨委定位成。把方向、管大局。作決策、保落實。地方黨委書記。主持黨委的全面工作。而市長通常同時兼任市委副書記。主持市政府的行政工作。也就是說。一個管整座城市。政治方向的黨內一把手。一個是負責把這套方向。執行出去的行政首長。誰在上、誰在下。制度一開始就已經安排好了。這也就是為什麼。不管市長在鏡頭前看起來有多威風。只要市委常委會一開。坐在正中間發號施令的。永遠都是書記。市長基本上只是兼任。市委副書記的執行長而已。既然權力是一把手。也就是書記說了算。出事的時候又會是誰來扛呢？我想這就是最耐人尋味的地方了。

今天我們就來聊聊這個。黨政雙軌制。到底是怎麼運行的。而他們又為什麼要採取。

這種制度呢？讓我們先從黨政雙軌制說起。一般人可能會聽不懂。黨政雙軌制是什麼東西。如果用現代企業的架構。來做個比喻的話。大家應該就比較好懂了。在淪陷區的地方治理體系裡。市委書記的角色。就像是董事長兼朝廷派來的監軍。而市長充其量就是個苦命的。總經理兼CEO。表面上看好像是。一起把整座城市給管好。但私底下的權力博弈。還有階級地位。可是差了10萬8千里。在體制裡有句名言叫。管錢的永遠搞不過管人的。我們先來看看掛名總經理的市長。他每天的行程總是排得滿滿的。在外面剪綵接見外賓。到處巡視工地。鏡頭面前是風光的不得了。他手上抓著整個市政府的荷包。管理財政局、交通局、工務局。這幫幹活的單位。幾百億的公帑預算。都是他在批的。但是你以為市長管錢就是老大嗎？走進沒有攝影機的市委大樓。真正的太上皇其實是市委書記。身為身為董事長兼監軍的書記。平常根本懶得去管哪裡要修橋。哪裡要鋪路這種行政雜事。書記只抓最核心的兩樣東西。看清政治風向。還有握緊人事大權。說白了就是管大局跟管人。市長再怎麼有錢。再怎麼會簽公文。但地方黨委掌握著。重要幹部的管理。任免跟推薦權。而市委書記又主持整個。市委的工作。所以財政局長、工務局長。這些重要幹部未來能不能往上走。絕對不只是市長。一個人就說了算的。市委才是真正繞不過去的權力核心。甚至市長自己未來。能不能更上一層樓。同樣離不開上級黨委。還有組織體系的考核。所以大陸官場。有一個非常現實的道理。管錢當然很有權力。但是如果另外一個人。連誰來管錢都能影響。那你說到底誰比較大呢？這難道是潛規則嗎？

其實不是。他們甚至把這套玩法寫成了一套。白紙黑字的標準流程。在官場裡叫三重一大制度。所謂的三重一大。說穿了就是重大決策。重要人事任免。重大項目安排。還有大額資金使用。當地方治理碰到這些。真正影響全局的事情時。往往就不再只是。市政府內部單純的行政決策。而必須按照黨委跟政府。各自的議事規則。進入集體決策、請示。或者政治把關的程序。那具體是怎麼操作的呢。市長底下的局處首長。會先花好幾個月做調研。寫評論報告。

接著市長召集各部門。開市政府常務會議。大家精打細算。熬夜把企劃案給生出來。這時候市長的手上。雖然拿著完整的執行方案。但他絕對不敢直接宣佈動工。因為他必須立刻換上。市委副書記的身份。乖乖把這份厚厚的案子。送進市委大樓。向市委書記「請示匯報」。當然不是全中國每個工程。都固定照著同一張流程圖走。不同城市、不同層級、不同金額。權限都可能不一樣。但是只要事情重要到。涉及全市發展方向。重大人事或政治風險。市委這一關。通常就不是行政首長。想繞就繞得過去的。

接下來才是重頭戲。市委書記會召開。由他主持的市委常委會。把市長的方案攤在桌上。帶著大家進行所謂的政治把關。還有集體討論。如果常委會最後形成決策。這個案子才算是真正取得。政治上的綠燈。但如果連書記主持的。市委這一關都過不了的話。市政府前面做了再多專業調研。也很難真的往下推。等常委會這裡。把大印蓋下去以後。皮球又踢回給市長。由市政府負責組織人馬。去拼命施工花錢落實。而且在幹活的過程中。市委的巡視跟督辦小組。還會時不時拿著放大鏡。在後面盯著看。看你有沒有偏離黨委。他一開始就規劃好的框框。所以你看看這套流程。完美演繹了什麼叫。政府調研提案。黨委拍板定案。政府苦幹執行。黨委在後監工的循環。市長在外面再威風。本質上也不過是在書記畫好的圈圈裡。拼命拉業績的打工人。想不到大家都是高級打工人。如果你以為這種權力階級。只存在於文件跟會議裡。那就太小看這套體系了。在對岸的官場生態裡。有一種東西叫。體制微表情。那些外人看來近乎強迫症。甚至有些可笑的排場細節。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析兩岸地方治理架構的本質差異，揭開中共體制下「市委書記」與「市長」之間權力階級的神秘面紗。
  • 透過生動的企業職位比喻與「三重一大」制度解說，讓艱澀的「黨政雙軌制」運作邏輯與決策流程變得易於理解。
  • 反思集權動員與民主問責的制度代價，探討「權力授權來源」如何決定官員究竟是「唯上是從」還是「以民為本」。

摘要

市長為何只是二把手？拆解黨政雙軌制

在自由地區，地方首長由公民直選產生並全權掌握地方資源；然而在中國大陸的政治體制中，表面上風光剪綵、掌握預算的市長，實質上僅是「二把手」，真正的「一把手」是市委書記。說故事的人指出，市長代表負責執行的政府行政機關，而市委書記則代表掌控政治方向與人事大權的共產黨委員會。用現代企業來比喻，市委書記好比兼任朝廷監軍的「董事長」，市長則只是負責幹活的「總經理兼CEO」，體現了體制內「管錢的永遠搞不過管人的」之現實。

三重一大與體制微表情：黨大於政的運作現實

這套階級機制並非潛規則，而是明文寫在名為「三重一大」的制度規範中。任何重大決策、重要人事、重大項目與大額資金，即便市政府完成詳盡的調研與規劃，也必須送交市委常委會接受政治把關，形成「政府調研提案、黨委拍板定案、政府苦幹執行、黨委在後監工」的權力循環。此外，官方新聞中的排序先後、座次安排等「體制微表情」，更隨時都在向外界宣示「黨大於政」的核心原則。

極致效率背後的死穴：一言堂、內耗與權責分離

黨政雙軌制雖具備「集中力量辦大事」的高動員力與推土機般的效率，卻也帶來難以抹滅的制度代價。首先是一把手權力失控，如同薄熙來時期的重慶模式，政治意識碾壓專業技術；其次是若黨政兩大領導不合，易陷入嚴重的派系內耗；更關鍵的是「權責分散」的甩鍋死結——決策是由閉門的黨委會拍板，司法與外部無從監督，但行政執行與日後的爛攤子、法律責任卻主要由行政首長承擔，外界難以釐清真實責任歸屬。

權力向誰負責：民主授權與民權主義的終極反思

說故事的人強調，兩套制度最根本的差異在於「授權方向」。自由地區首長的權力直接來自選民，做不好隨時會被選票拉下台；而對岸官員的政治前途取決於上級黨委的臉色，導致其決策必然「唯上是從」而非「以民為本」。這正呼應了國父孫中山先生所提出的「政權在民，治權在府」。唯有當地方首長的權力真正來自人民、只需看人民臉色時，才能走出體制怪圈，落實真正的共和與民權價值。

================================================

哈囉大家好。我是阿牛哥。今天要繼續來聊聊。兩岸制度上的差異。

今天想要跟大家聊的是。地方首長。在我們的自由地區。大家已經很習慣了。地方首長是由人民直選的。可以掌握整個地方的資源。但是在淪陷區就不是這樣。表面上市長去風光剪綵。出席活動。回到了辦公室。卻要看另外一個人的臉色。也就是市委書記。那問題來啦。

為什麼名義上是市府的最高長官。但卻只是二把手呢？在災區的權力架構裡。市長代表的是行政機關。也就是政府的系統。但市委書記。他代表的是共產黨委員會。也就是黨的系統。依照他們的規矩。黨是管方向、管人事、管大局的。政府只是負責執行黨的決策。而且這個黨領導政府。不是阿牛哥故意酸他們。更不是什麼官場上的潛規則。中共自己黨內法規。就把地方黨委定位成。把方向、管大局。作決策、保落實。地方黨委書記。主持黨委的全面工作。而市長通常同時兼任市委副書記。主持市政府的行政工作。也就是說。一個管整座城市。政治方向的黨內一把手。一個是負責把這套方向。執行出去的行政首長。誰在上、誰在下。制度一開始就已經安排好了。這也就是為什麼。不管市長在鏡頭前看起來有多威風。只要市委常委會一開。坐在正中間發號施令的。永遠都是書記。市長基本上只是兼任。市委副書記的執行長而已。既然權力是一把手。也就是書記說了算。出事的時候又會是誰來扛呢？我想這就是最耐人尋味的地方了。

今天我們就來聊聊這個。黨政雙軌制。到底是怎麼運行的。而他們又為什麼要採取。

其實不是。他們甚至把這套玩法寫成了一套。白紙黑字的標準流程。在官場裡叫三重一大制度。所謂的三重一大。說穿了就是重大決策。重要人事任免。重大項目安排。還有大額資金使用。當地方治理碰到這些。真正影響全局的事情時。往往就不再只是。市政府內部單純的行政決策。而必須按照黨委跟政府。各自的議事規則。進入集體決策、請示。或者政治把關的程序。那具體是怎麼操作的呢。市長底下的局處首長。會先花好幾個月做調研。寫評論報告。

Normally can't even be bothered to deal with which bridge needs repairing. or which road needs paving—that kind of administrative busywork. The secretary only grabs hold of the two most core things. See clearly which way the political wind is blowing. And firmly grasp the power over personnel. Put plainly, it means managing the big picture and managing people. No matter how much money the mayor has. No matter how good he is at signing official documents. The local Party committee still controls. The management of important cadres. The power to appoint, remove and recommend them. And the municipal party secretary also presides over the entire. work of the municipal party committee. So whether the finance bureau director, the public works bureau director. and other important cadres can move up in the future. is absolutely not something the mayor. alone gets to decide. The municipal party committee is the true core of power that cannot be bypassed. Even the mayor's own future. whether they can climb another rung. likewise cannot do without the higher-level Party committee.

and the assessment of the organizational system. so in mainland officialdom. there is a very realistic truth. those who control the money certainly have a lot of power. but if another person. can even influence who gets to control the money. So who do you think is actually more powerful? Is this some kind of unspoken rule? Actually, it's not. They've even written this whole way of doing things into a set of. standard procedures in black and white. In officialdom, it's called the "three importants and one large" system. The so-called "three importants and one large" simply put, means major decisions. important personnel appointments and removals. major project arrangements. and the use of large sums of funds. When local governance encounters these. matters that truly affect the overall situation. they often are no longer just. a simple administrative decision within the municipal government. but must follow the Party committee and the government. their respective rules of procedure. enter collective decision-making, request instructions. or political gatekeeping procedures. So how does it actually work in practice? The heads of bureaus and departments under the mayor. will first spend several months doing research. writing review reports. Then the mayor convenes all departments. Holds the municipal government executive meeting. Everyone crunches the numbers carefully. And stays up all night to produce the proposal. At this point, in the mayor's hands. Although he holds a complete implementation plan. He absolutely does not dare to directly announce the start of construction. Because he must immediately put on. The identity of deputy secretary of the municipal party committee. dutifully take this thick proposal. and send it into the Party Committee building. to "request instructions and report" to the Party Committee secretary. Of course, not every project in all of China. follows the same fixed flowchart. Different cities, different levels, different amounts of money. may all have different authorities. But as long as a matter is important enough to. involves the city's development direction. major personnel or political risks. this hurdle of the municipal Party committee. usually it is not something the chief administrative officer. can just bypass if he wants to. next comes the main event. the municipal Party secretary will convene. the Standing Committee of the Municipal Party Committee that he chairs. lays the mayor's proposal out on the table. leading everyone in what is called political gatekeeping. as well as collective discussion. If the Standing Committee ultimately reaches a decision. only then does this case truly obtain. the political green light. But if even the party committee. chaired by the secretary cannot get past this hurdle. No matter how much professional research the city government did beforehand. it's still very hard to actually push it through. Once the Standing Committee here. stamps its seal of approval. the ball gets kicked back to the mayor. and the city government is responsible for organizing the manpower. to go all out on construction and spend the money to implement it. And while the work is being done. The municipal party committee's inspection and supervision team. will also from time to time take out a magnifying glass. and stare at you from behind. to see whether you have deviated from the party committee's. framework that it had planned out from the very beginning. So just look at this whole process. It perfectly demonstrates what is meant by. the government researching and proposing. The Party committee makes the final call and settles the matter. The government grinds away at implementation. A cycle in which the Party committee supervises from behind. No matter how impressive the mayor looks on the outside. essentially, he is still just inside the circle the Party secretary drew. A worker desperately chasing performance numbers. Who'd have thought everyone is a senior-level worker. If you think this kind of power hierarchy. only exist in documents and meetings. then you've seriously underestimated this system. In the officialdom on the other side of the strait. there is something called. regime micro-expressions. Those details of pomp that to outsiders seem almost obsessive. even somewhat laughable. are in fact, every second. the four words of a silent oath. the Party is greater than the government. If everyone looks over the long term at local Party newspapers. official television news. they will find. news ordering, who chairs meetings. official name lists, seating order. usually place great importance on political ranking within the Party. The municipal party secretary often occupies the first position. while the mayor is placed further back. These seem like just minor details of etiquette. but in fact they are all local power. an external manifestation of the structure. Especially at large meetings. investment promotion events. or groundbreaking ceremonies for major projects. Clearly, a lot of administrative work is. handled by the city government team. but in the overall political narrative. the party committee is often still placed in. the position of leading the overall situation. This is not simply one official being more concerned about face; rather, it is the entire system. constantly reminding everyone. The administrative system can be very important. but in the end it still operates. under the leadership of the Party. So the Party is greater than the government. This is not just. an abstract principle written in documents. but is expressed through news ordering, seating arrangements, who presides. and everyday political etiquette. are constantly being reconfirmed. No matter how capable an administrative chief is. they can't forget who the number one in the Party really is. Seeing this, you might think. Since this system is so stifling. with so much red tape. why does the other side still use it? Is it really good for nothing? From a rational analysis standpoint. this dual-track party-government system. has been able to operate on the other side for so many years. and even drove, over the past few decades. an astonishing economic explosive power. Behind it, there really is an extremely domineering. yet highly efficient operating logic. This system's formidable killer move. the super-strong mobilization power of concentrating forces to accomplish big things. the super-strong mobilization power. In an ordinary administrative bureaucratic system. the various ministries and agencies often form their own fiefdoms. passing the buck to one another. which is commonly known as. "fragmentation along vertical and horizontal lines" But the party committee secretary is different.

He represents the highest authority of the party. They can not only call on the police. the propaganda department and the prosecutorial system. but also directly coordinate the local state-owned enterprises. and bank treasuries. when the party secretary gives the order to rush construction. of a major industrial park. build a cross-sea bridge. or when a major crisis occurs. he can instantly cut through. all the cumbersome paperwork processes. and throw the entire city's resources. all at the same goal. The mayor is responsible for crunching the finances and driving execution. the party secretary is responsible for steering from above. and clearing away all obstacles. the model of "politics steers, administration rows" When everything is going smoothly. it really shows a bulldozer efficiency. that Western bureaucracies find hard to imagine. But this kind of flooring the gas pedal. high-speed operation. the institutional price paid behind it. and the dark costs are equally staggering. We only need to look back. real historical major political scandals that actually happened. and it will be crystal clear. The first fatal flaw is. the top leader's power running out of control. Political consciousness directly overrides professional expertise. because the party secretary is the absolute core within the jurisdiction. the discipline inspection commission and people's congress at the same level. even the mayor. are all his subordinates in the party hierarchy. It is extremely easy for this to turn into. one person having the final say on personnel and one pen controlling all spending. a local emperor model. One of the most classic examples is Chongqing back then. During Bo Xilai's tenure as municipal party secretary. Chongqing vigorously promoted singing red songs and cracking down on organized crime. And also, also his series of. governance measures with a strong political coloration. The city government, in turn, must align with the Party committee's political direction. handling finances. land investment. construction, and day-to-day administration. What this case truly deserves our attention for. is not trying to guess what the mayor thinks in his heart. whether he actually agrees with the Party secretary or not. but rather that when a locality's top leader. When someone holds extremely strong political authority. no matter how many. professional and technical bureaucrats there are in the administrative system. how much professional judgment they can exercise. is still enormously constrained by the overall political direction. When the municipal party secretary inflates party power. into personal arbitrary rule. even the most outstanding within the administrative system. economic and technical bureaucrats. can only be reduced to cash machines for political fanaticism. and bulldozers. until the entire Chongqing model. completely collapsed along with the Wang Lijun incident. and Bo Xilai was thrown in prison. Huang Qifan, because he adhered to principles. narrowly escaped it. But still, all he could do was stay behind to clean up the mess. The second fatal flaw is. the two parallel centers of power, the Party and the government. If they don't get along. it can instead produce enormous internal friction. Nanjing has seen this happen before. Yang Weize, Secretary of the Municipal Party Committee, and Ji Jianye, Mayor. had a long-term strained relationship. The two later, one after the other. fell from power due to corruption problems. The institutional problem these kinds of cases truly reflect is. when the two principal leaders of the municipal party committee and the municipal government. each hold different political and administrative resources. but there is also a lack of transparent, open. and arbitrable by the people. power competition mechanism. policy disagreements can easily. go from a simple difference of administrative opinion. to a factional, personnel and political power struggle. in the end. the one who truly suffers is often the entire city. but the deeper contradiction lies in how modern society. demands administration in accordance with the law. every move the government makes. should all be subject to the supervision of the law and the courts. But under this dual-track system. the most core decisions. are all made in closed-door party committee meetings. the judicial system outside cannot reach them at all. Internal party documents and directives. This causes major decisions to often be. finalized by the municipal party committee. But the ensuing fiscal deficits. the messes left behind, or the environmental damage. are mainly borne by the chief executive. This kind of decision-making hides within the Party. and the blame is dumped on the administration. In this mode of operation, the law is completely powerless against it. Add to that a top leader who is too strong. and it will degenerate into a one-voice chamber. If both deputies are strong. they fall into a vicious cycle of internal friction and mutual biting. This is this centralized system. while pursuing extreme efficiency. a systemic dead knot that can never be untied. As mentioned earlier. whether it was Bo Xilai or the vicious struggle in Nanjing. at least everyone was fighting for credit and territory. But what really exposes them. is whenever there's a mistake or a major incident. how this system shifts the blame. Once a major disaster occurs. a safety accident or a governance failure. of course the administrative system must be held responsible. The Party committee system. in theory also bears leadership responsibility. So it cannot simply be understood as. the mayor definitely taking the blame. and the party secretary always getting off scot-free. But what is truly noteworthy is. under the structure of the dual party-government track. who actually proposed a policy. who made the final decision in the party committee. and who is responsible for administrative execution. And in the end, who should bear the political responsibility? often is not like democratic local governments. easy for outsiders to see clearly. Major decisions. may first take shape within the Party committee system. but the ones who actually sign administrative orders. draw up budgets, and carry out construction and implementation. are the city government. By the time problems arise with something. the first batch of people the outside world sees as specifically responsible. often turns out to be the administrative agencies again. This creates a question that is very much worth. thinking about. Power is dispersed between the party and the government. within these two systems. so how should responsibility be precisely matched up? So the real institutional deadlock. may not be that the party secretary bears no responsibility at all. but that decision-making power and administrative power. political responsibility and legal responsibility.

are split across two different systems. When an ordinary citizen wants to ask. who exactly made this decision. the answer may be far more complicated than we imagine. If everyone looks back again. at local governance in our free region. you'll discover the essence of the two systems. exactly where the difference lies. Of course. I'm not saying local politics in the free region. is some perfect paradise. Taiwan's mayors are the same. may pass the buck, put on a show, and build factions. the party center will also apply pressure. in the council, there will still be horse-trading. local governments can likewise see. corruption and scandals. even administrative failure. Democracy. has never guaranteed that the people we elect. are all surely saints. What democracy truly guarantees is something else. When he is not a saint. we have institutions to deal with him. On the land of liberal democracy. the mayor we elect. He bears the power, and he also compiles the budget. Are the roads paved smooth? Was flood prevention done well during typhoons? That ballot in the voter's hand. is the most direct judgment. If he does well, citizens give him applause for reelection. If he does poorly or even a major corruption scandal breaks out. he has to stand in the council himself. and face the councilors' harsh questioning. and bow in apology to all citizens in front of the cameras. In the next election, they'll be voted out by the voters. and swept right out the door. Actually, putting the two sides together for comparison. the most interesting thing isn't whether Taiwan's mayor. has more power. It's that the direction of authorization in the two systems. is fundamentally different. Local heads of government in free regions. The most direct political mandate comes from the voters. In the fallen region, the mayor. although formally. elected by the people's congress at the same level. the region's highest political leader. the party committee secretary. whose real political career and source of power. come mainly from the Communist Party's own organization. within the higher-level Party committee system. So the most fundamental difference between the two sides. can be condensed into one sentence. The power in one system. is mainly sought downward for authorization. officials in the other system. rather need to obtain political recognition upward. When an official's promotions and disgrace. is not held in the hands of the people. on the land beneath our feet. but instead depends on the backing of. that party secretary who holds the power of life and death over personnel. and on the expressions of the higher-level party committee. then all of his decisions will naturally follow only what is above. rather than being people-centered. in their eyes, the common people. are nothing but a backdrop for the sprint to pad performance statistics. or when something goes wrong and it's time to write a self-criticism report. just cold, lifeless casualty numbers. So in the end. what this video really wants to discuss. is actually no longer. who is more powerful, the municipal party secretary or the mayor? The real question is. The greatest power in this city. who exactly gave it to him? And the person who holds that power. who ultimately must he answer to? If we zoom out and look at the bigger picture. we'll discover that this absurd cycle of power. actually, more than 100 years ago. when the Founding Father, Sun Yat-sen, proposed the Three Principles of the People. has already provided the most thorough solution. So in the end. the truly important question is? That greatest power. who exactly gave it to him. In the CCP system. what local officials really need to care about is. how the higher-level Party committee sees him. how the organizational system evaluates him. whether his political line is on the right side. This is in fact the very core of the Principle of Democracy. the single most central thing. The Founding Father divided the nation's rights into. political power and governing power. Political power belongs to the people. governing power is handed to the government. The people don't need to go out and pave the roads themselves every day. build the MRT, or calculate the government budget. We hire a professional government to handle things for everyone. But handing things over to the government to handle. doesn't mean we become the government's subjects. Our system is certainly not perfect. We're still arguing every day too. But at least today. A mayor of the Republic of China. no matter how much power he holds. when the four years are up. in the end, he still has to. stand before the people again and ask. whether you are willing to continue. entrusting this right to me. This is the simplest. and the most profound meaning. Today, in the free area. it has already been proven. that Chinese society can do this. We can elect mayors. we can recall politicians. we can allow political parties to rotate in power. we can openly criticize the government every day. No matter how much the government dislikes the people's voices. it cannot, just because you voted the wrong way. or said the wrong thing. strip you of your status as the master of the country. This is what is most precious about Free China. And what the National Revolution has truly not yet completed. is precisely this. No matter which political party. Which piece of land is ruled again. No matter which flag. Is planted again in which city. But rather. That one day, let the mainland region. The people of every city. Also truly be able to decide. Who gets to be my mayor. who uses my tax money. whoever does a bad job. I can call for them to step down. When that day comes. what local leaders truly need to look at. will no longer be the Party secretary's mood. but the mood of the people. This is what civil rights truly means. This is what a republic truly is. This is the free China everyone envisions.

The political cause of the National Revolution. Though beset by countless trials and setbacks, it will never cease.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zXsWQVNUCrY

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析兩岸地方治理架構的本質差異，揭開中共體制下「市委書記」與「市長」之間權力階級的神秘面紗。
  • 透過生動的企業職位比喻與「三重一大」制度解說，讓艱澀的「黨政雙軌制」運作邏輯與決策流程變得易於理解。
  • 反思集權動員與民主問責的制度代價，探討「權力授權來源」如何決定官員究竟是「唯上是從」還是「以民為本」。

摘要

市長為何只是二把手？拆解黨政雙軌制

在自由地區，地方首長由公民直選產生並全權掌握地方資源；然而在中國大陸的政治體制中，表面上風光剪綵、掌握預算的市長，實質上僅是「二把手」，真正的「一把手」是市委書記。說故事的人指出，市長代表負責執行的政府行政機關，而市委書記則代表掌控政治方向與人事大權的共產黨委員會。用現代企業來比喻，市委書記好比兼任朝廷監軍的「董事長」，市長則只是負責幹活的「總經理兼CEO」，體現了體制內「管錢的永遠搞不過管人的」之現實。

三重一大與體制微表情：黨大於政的運作現實

這套階級機制並非潛規則，而是明文寫在名為「三重一大」的制度規範中。任何重大決策、重要人事、重大項目與大額資金，即便市政府完成詳盡的調研與規劃，也必須送交市委常委會接受政治把關，形成「政府調研提案、黨委拍板定案、政府苦幹執行、黨委在後監工」的權力循環。此外，官方新聞中的排序先後、座次安排等「體制微表情」，更隨時都在向外界宣示「黨大於政」的核心原則。

極致效率背後的死穴：一言堂、內耗與權責分離

黨政雙軌制雖具備「集中力量辦大事」的高動員力與推土機般的效率，卻也帶來難以抹滅的制度代價。首先是一把手權力失控，如同薄熙來時期的重慶模式，政治意識碾壓專業技術；其次是若黨政兩大領導不合，易陷入嚴重的派系內耗；更關鍵的是「權責分散」的甩鍋死結——決策是由閉門的黨委會拍板，司法與外部無從監督，但行政執行與日後的爛攤子、法律責任卻主要由行政首長承擔，外界難以釐清真實責任歸屬。

權力向誰負責：民主授權與民權主義的終極反思

說故事的人強調，兩套制度最根本的差異在於「授權方向」。自由地區首長的權力直接來自選民，做不好隨時會被選票拉下台；而對岸官員的政治前途取決於上級黨委的臉色，導致其決策必然「唯上是從」而非「以民為本」。這正呼應了國父孫中山先生所提出的「政權在民，治權在府」。唯有當地方首長的權力真正來自人民、只需看人民臉色時，才能走出體制怪圈，落實真正的共和與民權價值。

哈囉大家好。我是阿牛哥。今天要繼續來聊聊。兩岸制度上的差異。

這種制度呢？讓我們先從黨政雙軌制說起。一般人可能會聽不懂。黨政雙軌制是什麼東西。如果用現代企業的架構。來做個比喻的話。大家應該就比較好懂了。在淪陷區的地方治理體系裡。市委書記的角色。就像是董事長兼朝廷派來的監軍。而市長充其量就是個苦命的。總經理兼CEO。表面上看好像是。一起把整座城市給管好。但私底下的權力博弈。還有階級地位。可是差了10萬8千里。在體制裡有句名言叫。管錢的永遠搞不過管人的。我們先來看看掛名總經理的市長。他每天的行程總是排得滿滿的。在外面剪綵接見外賓。到處巡視工地。鏡頭面前是風光的不得了。他手上抓著整個市政府的荷包。管理財政局、交通局、工務局。這幫幹活的單位。幾百億的公帑預算。都是他在批的。但是你以為市長管錢就是老大嗎？走進沒有攝影機的市委大樓。真正的太上皇其實是市委書記。身為身為董事長兼監軍的書記。平常根本懶得去管哪裡要修橋。哪裡要鋪路這種行政雜事。書記只抓最核心的兩樣東西。看清政治風向。還有握緊人事大權。說白了就是管大局跟管人。市長再怎麼有錢。再怎麼會簽公文。但地方黨委掌握著。重要幹部的管理。任免跟推薦權。而市委書記又主持整個。市委的工作。所以財政局長、工務局長。這些重要幹部未來能不能往上走。絕對不只是市長。一個人就說了算的。市委才是真正繞不過去的權力核心。甚至市長自己未來。能不能更上一層樓。同樣離不開上級黨委。還有組織體系的考核。所以大陸官場。有一個非常現實的道理。管錢當然很有權力。但是如果另外一個人。連誰來管錢都能影響。那你說到底誰比較大呢？這難道是潛規則嗎？

其實每一秒都在。無聲的宣誓四個字。黨大於政。大家如果長期去看地方黨報。官方電視新聞。會發現。新聞排序、會議主持。官方名單、座次。通常都非常重視黨內的政治排名。市委書記往往居於第一順位。市長則排在後面。這些看起來只是禮儀的小細節。

第二個死穴就是。黨政兩套權力中心。如果彼此不和。反而可能產生巨大的內耗。南京過去就曾經出現。市委書記楊衛澤跟市長季建業。長期關係緊張的情況。兩人後來也先後。因為貪腐問題而落馬。這類案例真正反映的制度問題是。當市委與市政府兩位主要領導人。都握有不同的政治與行政資源。但彼此又缺乏透明、公開。而且可以由人民仲裁的。權力競爭機制時。政策分歧就很容易。從單純的行政意見不同。變成派系人事與政治上的角力。
